operation.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a paginated list of attendance logs for the account. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

The trailing path segment (`1`) is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page number. On this endpoint the data level has no visible effect, so `/attendance_log/list` and `/attendance_log/list/1` return the same result. Pagination is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters.

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `filter[<field>][<operator>]` | Filter by a field (see the Filterable fields table below). |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`. |
| `fields[]` | Restrict the returned columns. |

**Filterable fields.** Filter with `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`. The fields intended for filtering:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `staff_id` | integer (staff) | `filter[staff_id][equal]=1` |
| `status` | enum | `filter[status][equal]=draft` |
| `source_type` | enum (`machine`, `supervisor`, `file`, `self`) | `filter[source_type][equal]=self` |

In practice the endpoint accepts a filter on any existing column.

**Sorting.** Sort with `sort[<field>]=asc|desc` (e.g. `sort[time]=desc`). No field is specifically flagged as sortable in the metadata, but the endpoint accepts a sort on any existing column; with no `sort`, results are returned newest-first.

The response is a standard paginated envelope; each item in `data` is a flat attendance-log record.

Each record's `status` is one of:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| draft | Draft |
| sign_in | Sign In |
| sign_out | Sign Out |
| repeated_sign_in | Repeated Sign In |
| repeated_sign_out | Repeated Sign Out |
| invalid | Invalid |
| unknown_employee | Unknown Employee |

and `source_type`, when present, is one of `machine`, `supervisor`, `file`, `self`.

200.description: A paginated list of attendance logs.

data.description: The attendance logs on this page. Each item is an attendance-log record.

staff_id.description: Id of the employee the log belongs to.

session_id.description: Id of the attendance session, when applicable.

status.description:
Log status.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| draft | Draft |
| sign_in | Sign In |
| sign_out | Sign Out |
| repeated_sign_in | Repeated Sign In |
| repeated_sign_out | Repeated Sign Out |
| invalid | Invalid |
| unknown_employee | Unknown Employee |

source_id.description: Id of the source that produced the log, when applicable.

source_name.description: Name of the source, when applicable.

source_type.description:
Source of the log.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| machine | Machine |
| supervisor | Supervisor |
| file | File |
| self | Self |

source_method.description: How the source recorded the log, when applicable.

invalidity_reason.description:
Why the log is invalid, when applicable.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| weekend | Weekend |
| on_leave | On Leave |
| no_shift | No Shift Assigned |
| out_of_shift_boundaries | Out of Shift Boundaries |

400.description: The list could not be produced — for example the attendance-log entity is unavailable for this account or the required plugin is inactive.

error.description: Reason the request failed (e.g. the attendance-log entity is unavailable for the account, or the required plugin is not active).

401.description: Authentication or authorization failed. A missing, invalid, or expired Bearer token returns a plain `401` (no JSON body). An authenticated caller who lacks permission to view attendance logs receives `{ "error": "You are not allowed to view this page" }`.
